correctness.rationale: Exact block stationarity gives a linear (m+1)-state iteration with an (m−1)-fold disagreement eigenvalue and explicit 2-by-2 sum/dual block. Jury inequalities give the necessary-and-sufficient strict stability threshold, including nonconvergent boundary eigenmode. The spectral minimum is uniquely where strictly decreasing negative sum/dual modulus intersects strictly increasing disagreement modulus. For s≥m−1 both sum/dual eigenvalues have modulus less than disagreement. Algebra and exact rational finite checks verified from a standalone program; they do not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: Closest directly matching primary literature (He–Xu–Yuan 2013) proves only general sufficient s≥m−1 for proximal Jacobi and states the smaller-coefficient question; the exact all-initial scalar threshold, unique spectral minimizer and leading factor 4/3 are not its stated results. Recent Maia–Monteiro–Silva concerns a different safeguarded adaptive scheme; other closest items are sequential or under-relaxed. Priority remains best-knowledge and unverified independently.
residual_risks: Historical literature may contain equivalent eigenvalue optimization under a different proximal splitting nomenclature; searches and accessible principal texts are not an exhaustive priority proof.
The exact source algorithm is a known classical method; only the sharp homogeneous spectral classification is proposed as new.
All claims are restricted to unit, identical scalar blocks and an unrelaxed dual update.

value.rationale: The classical full-Jacobi proximal coefficient recommendation s=m−1 suppresses potentially unstable coupled dual/sum modes but over-damps disagreement. The exact global stable threshold and unique signed-mode balancing parameter show a nontrivial operating regime previously outside the general sufficient guarantee; the factor 4/3 in the large-block spectral gap quantifies the practical structural tradeoff on a natural all-block strongly convex quadratic, not a cosmetic substitution.
